name: Cavern Water Table
desc: A limestone chamber lit from below — four curtains of fluted stalactites hang out of a lost ceiling into a still, glowing water table, and the water throws a slow net of caustic light back up onto the stone so every form is modelled from underneath; drips swell at the tips, fall, strike and open rings that die away in the dark. Cool flowstone, a turquoise cenote, one carbide lamp, a stippled engraving plate, or a low-poly faceted crystal shell.

energy.doc: how hard the water burns — caustic net intensity, drip brightness and overall contrast

scale.doc: how far the stalactites reach down toward the water (rebuilds every curtain)

density.doc: how many stalactites hang per curtain, and how fine the caustic net is

wet.doc: how live the formation is — how brightly the wet tips catch the light from below

glow.doc: how much light is in the water, and how far the far chamber glows

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default cold flowstone / blue water

x.doc: where the light in the water sits across the chamber

y.doc: the water table — low y floods the chamber and shortens every stalactite

style.doc: aesthetic: limestone = cool grey-cream flowstone over lit water, sacred and enormous; cenote = warm ochre rock and impossible turquoise, daylight leaking from a far dome; carbide = one caver's lamp, dark key, the chamber only implied; stipple = a steel-engraved grotto plate, tone entirely from stipple and hatch with no fills; lowpoly = the cave as a triangulated faceted shell, hard flat-shaded crystal

act.doc: multi-minute programme — a steady drip, a flood pulse quickening it, or the cave going silent

seed.doc: regenerates the curtains, the flutes and which tips carry drips

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
